title: Abductive Learning for Neuro-Symbolic Grounded Imitation

problem.claim: Long-horizon planning in open environments requires imitation methods to handle observation-action learning and symbolic reasoning across high-dimensional visual inputs.

gap.claim: Learning-to-imitation methods are constrained in open environments, while traditional symbolic planning struggles with high-dimensional visual inputs.

contributions.claim: The work introduces ABductive Imitation Learning (ABIL), a framework integrating data-driven learning with symbolic-based reasoning for long-horizon planning.
ABIL uses abductive reasoning to interpret demonstrations in symbolic space and sequential consistency principles to resolve conflicts between perception and reasoning.
ABIL generates predicate candidates without laborious predicate annotations and uses a symbolically managed policy ensemble with base policies organized around different logical objectives.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe ABIL as a novel framework.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments demonstrate that ABIL comprehends observations with task-relevant symbolics to aid imitation learning.
The authors report improved data efficiency and generalization across various long-horizon tasks.

narrative_sequence.summary: Existing imitation methods face limitations in open environments and long-horizon tasks.
Symbolic planning handles long-horizon tasks through logical reasoning but has difficulty with real-world visual inputs.
ABIL combines data-driven learning and symbolic reasoning, using abductive reasoning and sequential consistency.
The framework generates predicate candidates and manages a policy ensemble through symbolic reasoning.
The authors report task-relevant symbolic understanding, improved data efficiency, and improved generalization across long-horizon tasks.

source_observation.claim: Combining symbolic representations with data-driven imitation is presented as a way to support long-horizon planning from visual observations.

interpretation.claim: A hybrid representation may address complementary weaknesses of purely observation-action imitation and purely symbolic planning.

application.claim: For long-horizon tasks in visually rich environments, consider intermediate symbolic representations and reasoning-guided policy composition.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish how the approach performs outside the reported task settings or under alternative representation and reasoning designs.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify datasets, baselines, quantitative results, or experimental protocols.
The abstract does not describe the implementation details of abductive reasoning, sequential consistency, predicate generation, or policy management.
The abstract does not establish independent verification or reproducibility.
